panels.description: Navpur street, outside Lakshmi Stores. Mr. Rao, angry, waving his phone. SMS on screen.

lines.speaker: rao
lines.text: Every day, these messages! And they refused me credit last week.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: So what's the plan?

lines.speaker: rao
lines.text: Ten complaints to the Data Protection Board. "Lakshmi Stores leaked my data." One in my name, the rest in my cousin Suresh's name. They'll panic.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Did they actually leak your data?

lines.speaker: rao
lines.text: No. But they don't know that.

options.label: Help him fill in the complaints
Tell him what he can really do

panels.description: Phone screen: a letter from the Data Protection Board to Mr. Rao.
panels.caption: Six weeks later.

panels.description: Mr. Rao, surprised. Nyay appears, worried.

lines.speaker: rao
lines.text: Costs? On ME?

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Citizens have duties too. A false complaint, or one in someone else's name, can cost you. The Board can also fine a person up to ₹10,000 for breaking these duties.

panels.description: Phone screen: Meera gets a call from an unknown number.
panels.caption: A week later.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: I should have said something.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Staying quiet let him use another person's name.

panels.description: Navpur street. Meera, neutral, with Mr. Rao, angry.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: You don't want the offers? That's a real complaint. Tell the shop, in your own name. You can take back your consent for the messages.

lines.speaker: rao
lines.text: And if I just make it sound worse?

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: The law gives people duties as well as rights: follow the law, don't pretend to be someone else, don't hide facts when you apply for government IDs, don't file false or frivolous complaints, and give only true details when you ask for a correction.

options.label: Mr. Rao writes to Lakshmi Stores in his own name, withdrawing consent for the offers
Mr. Rao asks the shop to "correct" his number to Suresh's, so the offers go there

panels.description: Phone screen: Rao's message to Lakshmi Stores. Nyay floats in front of it, worried.
panels.caption: That's Suresh's number.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Correction means fixing what's wrong, with true details. Putting in someone else's number isn't a correction.

lines.speaker: rao
lines.text: Fine, fine.

lines.speaker: rao
lines.text: That was easy. No cousin needed.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: And no costs either.

panels.description: Ammamma's home. Ammamma, neutral, with Meera.

lines.speaker: ammamma
lines.text: After the hospital business, I've been thinking. One day I may not manage these things myself. Who will, then?

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: You can choose someone. It's called nominating.

panels.description: Phone screen: CureWell's Privacy Centre. Fields: nominee's name, relationship, phone.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: A nominee steps in only if Ammamma dies, or can't act because of illness of mind or body. Until then, it's still her call.

options.label: Ammamma nominates Meera through the Privacy Centre
Ammamma just gives Meera her passwords instead

panels.description: Ammamma, happy, holding out a notebook of passwords. Nyay, worried.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Sharing passwords isn't nominating. It gives Meera no legal right, and it puts every one of Ammamma's accounts at risk.

lines.speaker: ammamma
lines.text: Then let's do it properly.

panels.description: Meera's room by day. Meera, worried, looking at her calendar. The note is marked: two months ago.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Thirty days, they said. Not a word.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Then you've given the company its chance. It's time for the Board.

board_letter.body: The Board finds your complaint against Lakshmi Stores to be false: there was no data breach. The Board has issued a warning and imposed costs on you. Filing complaints in another person's name also goes against your duties under the Act.

suresh_call.text: This is Suresh, Rao's cousin. Someone filed complaints with the Data Protection Board in MY name. Do you know anything?

messages.text: Please correct my phone number to 98XXX XXXXX.

lakshmi_reply.text: Done, Mr. Rao. No more offers. Your loyalty points are still there if you want them.

curewell_nominate.text: Nominate a person who can use your data rights if you pass away or can no longer act for yourself.

grievance_reminder.calendar: QuickPaisa grievance sent. Reply promised within 30 days.

CS20.question: Do ordinary people have any duties under India's data protection law?
options: Yes, such as not filing false complaints or pretending to be someone else
CS20.explanation: Breaking these duties can lead to a warning, costs, or a fine of up to ₹10,000.

LS21.question: Mr. Rao filed a false complaint in his own name and others in his cousin's name. What can follow?
shortAnswerOptions: Nothing, because only Data Fiduciaries have duties
A warning or costs, and a penalty of up to ₹10,000 for breaching s. 15
LS21.modelAnswer: s. 15(b) bars impersonating another person while providing personal data, and s. 15(d) bars registering a false or frivolous grievance or complaint with a Data Fiduciary or the Board. Under s. 28(12), at any stage after receiving a complaint, the Board may issue a warning or impose costs on a complainant whose complaint is false or frivolous. Breach of s. 15 duties also carries a penalty of up to ₹10,000 (Schedule item 5), which the Board may impose under s. 33 after an inquiry finds the breach significant.

CS21.question: Mr. Rao keeps getting offers he never wanted from a shop's app. What's the right first step?
options: Complain to the Board in his cousin's name
Ask the shop, in his own name, to stop
Exaggerate the problem so they take it seriously
CS21.explanation: Take back your consent and tell the company first, honestly and as yourself.

LS22.question: Which of these is NOT a duty of a Data Principal under s. 15?
shortAnswerOptions: Not suppressing material information when applying for a State-issued ID or proof of address
Not filing false or frivolous complaints
Reading every privacy notice before consenting
LS22.modelAnswer: s. 15 lists five duties: (a) comply with all applicable laws while exercising rights; (b) not impersonate another person while providing personal data; (c) not suppress material information when providing personal data for a document, unique identifier, proof of identity or proof of address issued by the State; (d) not register a false or frivolous grievance or complaint; and (e) furnish only verifiably authentic information when exercising the right to correction or erasure. There is no duty to read notices; the burden of a clear notice is on the fiduciary (s. 5, Rule 3).

LS23.question: Mr. Rao asks the shop to "correct" his phone number to his cousin's. Is that a valid correction request?
LS23.modelAnswer: No. s. 12(2) obliges the fiduciary to correct inaccurate or misleading data, complete incomplete data and update data. Rao's number isn't wrong, and substituting another person's number isn't a correction. s. 15(e) requires a Data Principal to furnish only verifiably authentic information when exercising the right to correction, and using a third person's details also engages s. 15(b).

CS22.question: What does nominating someone do?
options: Lets them read your messages and accounts right away
Lets them use your data rights if you die or can no longer act for yourself
Nothing. Only lawyers can act for you
CS22.explanation: A nominee steps in only on death or incapacity. Sharing passwords is not the same thing.

LS24.question: Ammamma nominates Meera. When can Meera exercise Ammamma's rights?
shortAnswerOptions: Only if Ammamma dies or becomes unable to exercise her rights because of unsoundness of mind or infirmity of body
LS24.modelAnswer: s. 14(1) lets a Data Principal nominate any other individual to exercise her rights in the event of her death or incapacity. s. 14(2) defines incapacity as inability to exercise those rights due to unsoundness of mind or infirmity of body. Under Rule 14(4), she may nominate one or more individuals using the means and particulars the Data Fiduciary requires, in line with its terms of service and applicable law.

CF23.title: Your duties
CF23.plain: Follow the law, don't pretend to be someone else, don't hide facts for government IDs, don't file false or frivolous complaints, and give only true details when you ask for corrections.

CF24.title: False complaints cost you
CF24.plain: The Board can warn you or make you pay costs for a false or frivolous complaint, and fine you up to ₹10,000 for breaking your duties.

CF25.title: Choosing a nominee
CF25.plain: You can choose someone to use your data rights if you die or can no longer act for yourself because of illness of mind or body.

endings.title: A costly lesson
endings.caption: Mr. Rao got his offers stopped in the end, but only after the Board warned him and made him pay costs.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Rights come with duties. A false complaint wastes the Board's time and can cost you.

endings.title: Good neighbours
endings.caption: Mr. Rao's messages have stopped, and Ammamma has named Meera to speak for her data if she ever can't.

lines.speaker: nyay
lines.text: Honest complaints, and a plan for the future. That's using the law well.

endings.title: Unfinished business
endings.caption: Mr. Rao's messages have stopped, but Ammamma hasn't named anyone yet.

card.title: What Ammamma could still do
items: Nominate someone through each company's own process.
Never share passwords as a shortcut.
